To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cPAM inhibited anaerobic digestion by restraining the solubilizing, hydrolyzing, acidogenic, and methanogenic processes, and the degradation metabolites of cPAM were found to be acrylamide, polyacrylic acid, and acrylic acid, and they inhibited the anaerobic processes to different extents.

the presence of a cationic poly(acrylamide) flocculant in waste activated sludge deteriorated anaerobic digestion and the degradation products of cationic flocculant significantly affected the methane production.
cPAM significantly inhibited the anaerobic degradation of sludge and the inhibition was mainly due to the degradation products of cPAM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comprehensive study of cPAM degradation and its impact on anaerobic sludge digestion.
the effects of the degradation products of cPAM on the anaerobic sludge digestion.
the mechanisms of cationic polymer affecting anaerobic digestion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cPAM addition significantly inhibited the anaerobic sludge digestion process and decreased the methane production by inhibiting the hydrolysis, solubilization acidogenesis, and especially the methanogenesis.
cPAM not simply deteriorated methane production but also significantly affected the sludge anaerobioic digestion.
cPAM deteriorated methane production by significantly inhibiting the sludge solublization, hydrolyzation, acidogenesis, methanogenesis, and the degradation of its own.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cPAM deteriorates sludge anaerobically digestion due to its inhibition on the sludge hydrolysis, methanogenesis, and its own degradation.

cPAM inhibited sludge anaerobiose digestion through the following pathways: (1) cPAM was degraded to polyacrylic acid, acrylamide, and acrylic acid, and (2) the degradation products inhibited the solubilzation, hydrolysis and acidogenesis of sludge and methanogenesis of sludge fermentation.
cPAM not just inhibited the sludge digestion process but also deteriorated the digestion performance, which should be taken into consideration for sludge anaerobically digested systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of the flocculant cPAM significantly inhibited sludge anaerobio digestion, and the inhibition mechanism was mainly attributed to the degradation products of cPAM.
cPAM is not a good substrate for anaerobic digestion and that it can significantly affect sludge digestion.

the addition of 0.5-2 g/kg of cPAM to sludge anaerobiic digestion systems is not suggested, and the cPAM dosage should be kept below 1 g/kg in order to avoid a significant decrease in methane production.
